rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for fixing or mending something in everyday speech.

example.english: My phone broke, so I took it in for repair.
example.jyutping: bou6 din6 waa2 waai6 zo2 ngo5 ling1 heoi3 zing2

rows.note: Use this especially when repairing a damaged physical object, appliance, vehicle, or piece of equipment, often in a service context.

example.english: The washing machine is broken, so I’ll take it to the shop for repair.
example.traditional: 部洗衣機壞咗，我要拎去舖頭修理。
example.jyutping: bou6 sai2 ji1 gei1 waai6 zo2 ngo5 jiu3 ling1 heoi3 pou3 tau4 sau1 lei5

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the act or work of repairing something.

example.english: The repair of this computer will take a few days to finish.
example.traditional: 呢部電腦嘅維修要幾日先搞得掂。
example.jyutping: nei1 bou6 din6 nou5 ge3 wai4 sau1 jiu1 gei2 jat6 sin1 gaau2 dak1 dim6

rows.note: Use this for an item's need for repair or the amount of repair it requires.

example.english: The repair this car needs will cost quite a bit.
example.traditional: 部車嘅維修需要唔少錢。
example.jyutping: bou6 ce1 ge3 wai4 sau1 seoi1 jiu1 m4 siu2 cin2

rows.note: Use this for a physical patch or patched area that is the visible result of a repair.

example.english: There is a repair patch over the hole in my trousers.
example.jyutping: tiu4 fu3 go3 lung1 jau5 faai3 bou2 baa1
